'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**Syria missile strikes (February 2021)
***[[Israeli Air Force|Israel]] launches [[airstrike]]s in [[Syria]], Syrian forces responded late on Wednesday to "Israeli aggression" in the south of the country, according to state news agency [[SANA]]. [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/middle-east/1612386207-israel-reportedly-attacks-site-in-southern-syria (i24 News)]
*[[Mali War]]
**Nine [[Malian Armed Forces|soldiers]] are killed and six others are wounded during an ambush near the village of [[Boni, Mali|Boni]], [[Mopti Region|Mopti]], [[Mali]]. Twenty attackers are also killed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/3/at-least-nine-soldiers-killed-in-central-mali-ambush-army (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Four [[Tunisian Armed Forces|Tunisian soldiers]] are killed by a [[land mine]] during a [[counter-terrorism]] operation in Mount Mghila, central [[Tunisia]]. [https://www.barrons.com/news/4-tunisian-soldiers-killed-in-landmine-blast-ministry-01612357505?tesla=y (AFP via ''Barron's'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[Shortages related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[General Motors]] announces the suspension of operations at its [[General Motors Fairfax Assembly Plant|Fairfax]], [[CAMI Automotive|Ingersoll]], and [[San Luis Potosí Assembly|San Luis Potosí]] assembly plants due to a global shortage of [[semiconductor]]s. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20210203-general-motors-shuts-three-plants-due-to-semiconductor-shortage (AFP via RFI)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Wooroloo bushfire]]
**Over 70 homes are destroyed by a large [[wildfire]] in [[Western Australia]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-03/perth-hills-bushfire-number-of-homes-lost-revised-up-to-71/13115670 (ABC Australia)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****Spain reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in [[Catalonia]]. Experts believe that it has no relation to [[South Africa]], the variant's country of origin, and that it originated in Europe. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/sanidad/20210203/catalunya-detecta-caso-variante-sudafricana-11494846 (''El Periódico'')]
****[[Spain]] surpasses 60,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-02-spain-virus-death-toll-surges.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Czech Republic]] surpasses one million cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1802941 (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****The [[Government of Sweden|Swedish government]] announces that all travellers will be required to show a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 testing result]] within 48 hours of arrival beginning February 6 in order to prevent the spread of [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. Swedish citizens as well as foreign residents living in [[Sweden]] will be exempt from this rule. [https://www.thelocal.se/20210203/sweden-announces-decision-on-new-travel-restrictions (''The Local Sweden'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination programme in the United Kingdom]]
****The number of people who have been vaccinated against COVID-19 in the [[United Kingdom]] surpasses 10 million. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-02-03/covid-uk-reaches-hugely-significant-milestone-as-10-million-people-vaccinated-for-coronavirus (ITV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Japan]]ese [[House of Councillors (Japan)|House of Councillors]] passes a law that will introduce fines for people and businesses that do not comply with restrictions imposed to prevent the spread of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/02/03/national/bills-fines-antivirus-measure/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]]
****[[Kuwait]] will suspend entry for non-citizens for two weeks beginning February 7, due to an increase in COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/covid-19-kuwait-bans-entry-for-non-kuwaitis-for-two-weeks-effective-feb-7---press-conference-1.1612377455327 (Gulf News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****The [[Health Sciences Authority]] approves the use of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna vaccine]] for people aged above 18 in [[Singapore]], becoming the first country in [[Asia]] to do so. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/moderna-covid-19-vaccine-singapore-authorised-hsa-first-shipment-14103204 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] reports a record of 3,977 new confirmed cases and 12 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 313,626 and the nationwide death toll to 878. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/02/03/Coronavirus-UAE-detects-record-number-of-new-COVID-19-cases-12-deaths-in-24-hours (Al-Arabiya)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kansas]]
****[[Kansas]] reports its first case of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|UK variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in [[Ellis County, Kansas|Ellis County]]. [https://www.kansas.com/news/coronavirus/article248993555.html (''The Wichita Eagle'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[Medsafe]] provisionally approves the use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] in [[New Zealand]] with certain conditions. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/435725/pfizer-biontech-covid-19-vaccine-granted-provisional-approval-by-medsafe (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***[[GlaxoSmithKline]] and the German biotech firm [[CureVac]] sign an agreement worth 150 million [[euro]]s ([[United States dollar|$]]180.7 million) to develop a [[vaccine]] to counter many [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. The vaccine, which is subject to regulatory approval, is expected to be introduced in 2022. [https://www.marketwatch.com/amp/story/glaxosmithkline-curevac-team-on-covid-19-vaccines-2021-02-03 (''MarketWatch'')]
***Preliminary tests indicate that the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] may reduce transmission of COVID-19 and not simply prevent symptomatic infections. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/health/medical/astrazeneca-coronavirus-vaccine-reduces-transmission-study-shows/ar-BB1dlNmb?ocid=uxbndlbing (U.S. News & World Report via MSN)]
*[[2020–21 H5N8 outbreak]]
**Authorities in [[Brandenburg]], [[Germany]], cull 14,000 [[Turkey (bird)|turkey]]s due to an outbreak of [[H5N8]] bird flu on a farm in the [[Uckermark]] area. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-birdflu-germany/germany-culls-14000-turkeys-after-bird-flu-was-found-on-another-farm-idUSKBN2A30YX (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Guyana–Venezuela relations]], [[Guayana Esequiba|Guayana Esequiba dispute]]
**The [[Government of Venezuela|Venezuelan government]] releases the crew of two [[Guyana]]-flagged fishing vessels detained by the [[National Bolivarian Armed Forces of Venezuela|Venezuelan military]] in January for alleged [[Illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing|illegal fishing]] in the disputed [[Guayana Esequiba]] region. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210203-venezuela-frees-crew-of-two-seized-guyana-boats (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**The [[Myanmar Police Force|police]] file [[criminal charge]]s against overthrown de facto leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] for illegally importing communications equipment and seek her custody until February 15 as part of investigations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/3/myanmar-police-file-charges-against-suu-kyi-says-document (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Terrorism in Canada]]
**[[Public Safety Canada|Public Safety Minister]] [[Bill Blair (politician)|Bill Blair]] announces the designation of 13 groups as [[Organizations designated as terrorist by Canada|terrorist organizations]], including the [[American far-right]] group [[Proud Boys]] and [[white supremacist]] organizations such as the [[Russian Imperial Movement]], [[Atomwaffen Division]], and [[The Base (hate group)|The Base]]. In the process, Canada has become the first country to designate the Proud Boys as a [[terrorist]] organization. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/canada-proud-boys-terrorist-capitol-siege/2021/02/03/546b1d5c-6628-11eb-8468-21bc48f07fe5_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2021/02/03/canada-declares-proud-boys-terrorist-organization/4372307001/ (''USA Today'')]
*Fifteen people are arrested in [[Ethiopia]] over a plot to attack the [[United Arab Emirates]]' [[embassy]] in the capital [[Addis Ababa]]. Several other suspects, who were planning attacks against the UAE's [[diplomatic mission]] in [[Sudan]], are also arrested. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/3/ethiopia-arrests-15-people-over-uae-embassy-attack-plot (Al Jazeera)]

**[[Mario Draghi]] accepts the order from [[President of Italy|President]] [[Sergio Mattarella]] to form an "emergency [[government of Italy|government]]" after [[Giuseppe Conte]]'s resignation. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/02/03/world/europe/mario-draghi-italy-government.html?searchResultPosition=2 (''The New York Times'')]
